labels.name: Routing

labels.name: Driving
labels.description: Drive a car related issues

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
Accurate travel time estimation is an essential part of a modern navigation app, it is highly necessary.  Without useful travel times, Organic Maps cannot become the default travel app for any person.


**Problem Statement**
1) The current trip time estimates are highly inaccurate, even when there is no traffic, travel estimates are too optimistic and do not calculate realistic time required to travel.

2) When there is traffic, the estimates are even more problematic, essentially useless, other apps to estimate time.

**Criteria**
- Display traffic delays with blue, yellow and red on the route.
- Calculate accurate travel estimates.
- Include traffic data with downloaded offline maps.

Keeping the traffic data offline would mean that it would account for typical traffic patterns such as morning and evening commutes, which covers 90% of use cases.  But it would not cover the traffic accidents or road closures which happen sometimes.  Since the vast majority of trips can have accurate time estimates with offline data, it's a good option which does not require making the app be online.

items.title: Generate Wikipedia articles from offline Wikipedia dump

labels.name: Wikipedia
labels.description: Issues related to Wiki articles embedded in OM data files.

items.body:
There are several issues now with our current crawler implementation:
1. It is banned by Wiki servers because it DDoSes the API.
2. It takes a lot of time to get all summaries for several supported languages.
3. If we add more languages, the time increases even more.
4. As a result, now we are still using some old outdated articles we got in this spring.

A way better option is to download a dump of all Wiki articles for given languages and extract summaries from there directly.

Any volunteers for this task?

A list of supported languages and the output format can be checked in the existing implementation in `tools/python/descriptions`.

items.title: First app open, explain offline + map download

labels.name: Downloader
labels.description: Map dowloader

labels.name: UX
labels.description: User eXperience, an issue with usability

labels.name: UI
labels.description: User interface issues

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**Overview**
For the average person in the United States and Europe, where cell phone service coverage is really good and online maps are the primary navigation apps, offline maps are not as well known, and downloading maps within an app may be a new concept for many people.

**Problem Statement**
- When opening the app for the first time, there is no explanation for why something else needs to be downloaded, after the app has already been downloaded; this could be a confusing experience.  Not having clear information about why downloads are required, detracts average people from using the app for the first time and results in a number of uninstalls right after downloading.
- Apps don't typically ask for additional downloads unless they are add-ons or expansion purchases.  Asking to download without clarifying, may give the impression that additional modules are necessary just to run the app.


**Criteria**
_Location permission prompt_
- Update text of the OS prompt for location from [iOS] "Determining your location is necessary for navigation and for saving your recently traveled track" to:
"Location permission is necessary to see your location on the map and for navigation instructions." 

_Test Connection_
- Before displaying the download prompt, test the network connection and ensure map are available for download. If not available, display a message:
"Connection cannot be established"

_Automatic Download - 1st map_
- When zero maps have been downloaded (no maps are available on the device), no matter if this is the first launch of the app or not, automatically zoom into the current location and automatically start downloading the map without asking.
- Bugs: Under certain conditions, after giving permission to location, does not automatically zoom into the phone's location. 1) When turning off screen after location permission prompt is displayed and then getting back to the app to give permission, it does not zoom in. 2) Giving "Allow Once" permission, but not downloading the map, then getting back to the app, giving permission again, it does not zoom in to the location. 3) Potentially other conditions, needs more testing.

_Download progress - 1st map_
- During download explain offline maps and why a download is needed.
- Download In Progress prompt: 

_"**Offline Maps**_
_[country]_
_[region / metro area]_
_Downloading_
_[progress indicator]_
_Organic Maps uses maps downloaded to your phone for navigation and fast search without a cellular service._"
- The text "Offline Maps" should be just a little larger than the bold map name.
- Remove the download percentage number, too much detail, the progress circle indicator is enough to show progress.
- Test spacing required for texts, as different languages need more space than English, for example German or Russian.
- The progress circle indicator is 2 wide pixels, change it to 3 pixels to be consistent with other icons.

_Download prompt - 2nd map_
- After the first map was downloaded automatically, the next map download will required the person to press the download button.
- Display the following text to explain again the need for downloading: 

_"**Offline Maps**_
_Download to get started_
_Organic Maps uses maps downloaded to your device for navigation and fast search without a cellular service._

[country]
[state/province] - [area]
xxMB"

_Download progress - 2nd map_
_"**Offline Maps**_
_[country]_
_[region / metro area]_
_Downloading_
_[progress indicator]_

_To download maps for additional regions, zoom in to new areas on the map_"
- When at least two maps have been downloaded, display the standard message that does not include explanation text.

**Design**
https://www.figma.com/design/K26gHeLViIbsPAmsHigHk1/Organic-Maps---First-Open?node-id=2-15&t=T6uzhxQBh2XK9ESI-1

items.title: Automatic offline map updates (Wi-Fi only, user-controlled)

labels.name: Downloader
labels.description: Map dowloader

items.body:
Feature Request: Automatic Offline Map Updates (Wi-Fi only)

Problem
Organic Maps relies on offline data, but map updates must be performed manually.
This means many users end up navigating with outdated maps without noticing it.
Important OSM changes (new roads, corrected POIs, path updates, accessibility info) only reach the user if they remember to update maps manually.

Currently, there is no option for background or scheduled updates.

⸻

Why this feature is important

This feature improves safety, accuracy, and usability:
	•	Users always have current OSM data
	•	No dependency on accounts, servers, or tracking
	•	Reduces the risk of following outdated roads/paths
	•	No manual maintenance required
	•	Fits Organic Maps’ philosophy: privacy-first & offline-first

Because the update files are downloaded only via Wi-Fi, users stay in full control and avoid mobile data usage.

⸻

Proposed solution

Add an optional, disabled-by-default setting:

“Automatic map updates (Wi-Fi only)”

When enabled, Organic Maps would:
	•	Check for updated map files once per week
	•	Download updates only when connected to Wi-Fi
	•	Show a small notification (“Maps updated”)
	•	Skip large downloads when battery is low
	•	Allow manual updating at any time

Important principles:
	•	All logic runs locally
	•	No tracking, no user identification
	•	No background analytics
	•	No push-services
	•	Zero online accounts required

⸻

Additional optional settings
	•	“Ask before updating” → shows dialog before download
	•	“Update only selected countries/regions”
	•	“Download updates only when charging”

These settings keep the feature flexible and privacy-compliant.

⸻

Alternatives considered
	•	Manual updates → unreliable, often forgotten
	•	Background sync via cloud → violates the privacy model of Organic Maps
	•	Update reminders → helpful but inferior to automatic updates

⸻

Summary

An optional Wi-Fi-only automatic offline map update system would significantly improve accuracy and safety while maintaining Organic Maps’ strict privacy and offline principles.
This is a practical, realistic upgrade that enhances the user experience without adding complexity or requiring online accounts.

items.title: [search] Improve offline address formatting and matching
items.body:
## Summary

Shared offline address-search improvements, extracted from #13311 so search correctness can be reviewed independently of Android contacts integration. The dependent branch includes this prerequisite and its review fixes. Related: #11412.

- Handle recognized address formatting, explicit units, postal context, abbreviations, numbered streets, and compound civic identifiers without rewriting visible queries. International coverage is improved, not universal.
- Prefer exact mapped addresses over interpolated/nearby alternatives and unrelated POIs, including distant downloaded maps. Preserve useful alternate mapped addresses under their actual numbers.
- Carry mapped house/street identity through result generation instead of interpreting presentation names as addresses. Reuse existing DACH street-spelling normalization.
- Resolve through the existing offline search engine with serialized cancellation/priority handling. Wait for complete, non-cancelled results before accepting a unique address; ambiguous/missing addresses do not produce invented coordinates.
- Preserve explicit title/address presentation and the resolved coordinate without extra nearest-building snapping. Notify consumers on map-data changes even without viewport movement.
- Register shared sources and address-matcher tests in Xcode as well as CMake.

No custom coordinate estimator, Pelias/network geocoder, extra dataset, or map-format change is introduced. Existing OpenStreetMap address interpolation remains supported. Contact-provider preparation, permissions, caches, and markers remain in #13311.

The additional resolution API/scheduling layer remains open for architectural review; this is not a replacement geocoder.

## Verification

October 16 combined dependent build: 106 search unit tests, 243 map tests, all 110 search integration tests, and 126 Android Google debug/SDK unit tests passed. Separate lintAllModules, ARM64 Google debug native/APK builds, and packaged permission checks passed. These are combined-build results, not a claim that the standalone prerequisite app was separately built.

The installed Pixel 8 Pro build was manually checked for resolved-point presentation/coordinate consistency. Xcode source-phase references were structurally checked; an actual iOS build was not run on Linux. GitHub currently reports DCO passing; full CI is not claimed.

LLM tools were used to implement and review these changes.

items.body:
A route from Birmingham, Alabama to Key West, Florida.

All times were calculated on LG V30 (H932) with Android 9, no SD card.

- Avoid Motorway is on for each app.
- Avoid Toll Roads is on for each app.

Map Factor was most consistent/stable.

Magic Earth:
Bicycle = 6min 25 sec
Auto = 16 sec (offering 3 different routes).
The bicycle route was calculated incorrectly.

OSMAnd:
Auto = 42sec with one waypoint. OSM fails if calculating the direct route of this distance
Bicycle = 1 min 53sec
OSMand also has the worst search function for its own data!
OSMamd performance deteriorates with multiple route calculations. Rebooting the device gives an initial improvement in performance, more than just clearing the cache. 8 minutes 43 sec on 3rd recalculation and froze on 4th attempt without rebooting the device. Performed FC to end app.

Sygic:
Auto = 10sec
No bicycle option.

Map Factor:
Auto = 5sec
Bicycle= 28sec

items.title: Add custom user notes to saved places (offline POI notes)
items.body:
Feature Request: Custom Notes for Saved Places (Offline POI Notes)

Problem
Organic Maps allows saving places as favorites, but users cannot attach any personal notes to a location.
Many real-world situations require storing private information (e.g. “best parking spot”, “doctor closes at 18:00”, “quiet picnic area”), which should not be added to OpenStreetMap and must remain private and offline.

Currently, there is no way to add such custom notes to a saved place.

Why this feature is important
This function aligns perfectly with Organic Maps principles:
	•	Fully offline
	•	No tracking
	•	No account
	•	Maximum user privacy
	•	Better usability in daily life

Examples of use cases:
	•	Parking tips
	•	Personal reminders
	•	Custom location labels
	•	Notes for hiking routes
	•	Appointment information
	•	Private orientation hints

Other apps offer notes, but require online accounts or sync features.
Organic Maps could offer a unique offline-only implementation.

⸻

Proposed solution

Add a small editable text field to every saved favorite:
	•	Visible in the “Place Details” screen
	•	Editable during creation or later
	•	Stored locally on the user’s device
	•	Included in the existing KML backup/restore system
	•	Should allow a few paragraphs of text

UI idea:
	•	Button: “Add note”
	•	Field shown under the place name

⸻

Alternatives considered
	•	Using external note apps → inconvenient and not integrated
	•	Adding notes to OSM → inappropriate for private/personal details

⸻

Summary

A built-in, offline, private note-field for saved locations would significantly improve usability without compromising Organic Maps’ simplicity or privacy standards.

items.title: Unable to use app 100% offline
items.body:
The app proudly advertises that it can be used offline.

Quote from official website:

> Organic Maps is one of the few applications nowadays that supports 100% of features without an active Internet connection.

Sadly, this promise turned out to be false.

When I first launched the app, I was greeted with a message that forced me to download a global map before I can do anything. There was no way to bypass this message. I then went to the Help/FAQ of the website to find a workaround, like allowing me to manually install the missing map data, e.g. by moving files to the right directories or something. But … nothing.

## Possible solutions

There are 2 possible solutions I can think of:

1 Update the FAQ to include a manual how to manually install the map data without *ever* connecting Android to the Internet (even just stating which files must go where would be extremely helpful)
2) Remove the false promises from the website. No longer advertise Organic Maps as "100% offline"

Version: 2025.03.02-7.FDroid on Android 7.
